significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that, for internally recoverable facts, expression follows a query-conditioned relation between activation of a compact "k<=10" attention-head router and answer production, with causal reopening of that router recovering the answer without changing storage; this combines a form-(iii) predictive coupling with a form-(ii) causal mechanism. It would constrain explanations of the localization–editing disconnect documented by Hase et al. (2023, "Does Localization Inform Editing?") by predicting that within-fact variation across paraphrases tracks routing-head activity rather than MLP content, thereby establishing both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanistic storage-versus-routing decomposition. Verified-false and verified-true are distinguishable for the compact causal claim: failure would rule out a small attention-dominant router, although the fallback that "if routing proves diffuse we report a distributed gate rather than abandon the account" makes refutation of the broader gating narrative less informative. After topic substitution, the broad storage-versus-retrieval question alone merits only the topic median; the compact-head bound, attention/MLP decomposition, cross-query predictive relation, and selective causal recovery are the claim-specific reasons for scoring above it.

reach.justification: The claim hands over two named handles: "gate-head features = attention mass the top-k heads place on subject/attribute tokens" as a predictor or auditing probe, and interventions that amplify "gate-head attention to the subject token" or patch gate-head outputs. The predictor and inference-time intervention are ex ante relative to answer completion—they can flag or alter a likely retrieval failure before the final answer is emitted—rather than merely explaining an observed error afterward. Although heads would need re-identification per model, the asserted relation that expression tracks gate activation across facts, paraphrases, and GPT-J, Llama, and Qwen architectures predicts what recalibration should recover; downstream users include "knowledge-editing practitioners" and "reliability auditors," not only mechanism researchers. Topic substitution would not retain this score: the transferable predictor-plus-reversible-intervention package, rather than the general importance of knowledge retrieval, supplies the extra reach.
